core_obligations: Replace S by a localisation at a nonzero element so that S becomes regular, which is what the J-0 hypothesis allows (proof lines 11657-11660).
Apply generic flatness to make the map faithfully flat over a further localisation (proof lines 11660-11662).
Use descent of regularity along a faithfully flat map to conclude that R is regular, hence J-0 (proof lines 11662-11664).

difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the J-0 property, meaning that the regular locus is open, descends from a finite type extension of domains to the base, and the proof is an 8-line argument of two reductions. It first localises the target at a nonzero element so that the extension becomes regular, then applies generic flatness to make the extension faithfully flat over a further localisation, at which point the descent of regularity along a faithfully flat map gives the conclusion. Both reductions are performed by named statements of the Algebra chapter, and the localisations are chosen so that the hypotheses of those statements are met, which is where the brevity of the proof hides its content.
